method_notes: Ratings: Wikipedia '2026 United States Senate elections' Predictions table (wikitext read 2026-10-31T01:39Z); each column's date is the date shown in that column header. Inside Elections additionally read from its own JSON feed (last_updated 2026-10-29T13:05-05:00).

Poll averages: aggregate-poll tables on each state's Wikipedia race page (read 2026-10-31 ~02:00Z), which transcribe DDHQ, FiftyPlusOne, RealClearPolitics, Silver Bulletin, 270toWin (and Texas Tribune). Values were not re-checked on the aggregator pages (RCP/DDHQ block automated reads).
Split Ticket: raw Datawrapper datasets behind The Argument's model page (saved in veri/kaynak-ham/).

Markets: Polymarket gamma API and Kalshi public trade API, read-only GET via WebFetch (polymarket.com and kalshi.com are DNS-blocked from this machine in Turkey; the block was not bypassed locally). Prices are implied probabilities; D and R contracts are separate books and need not sum to 1.
Nebraska: challenger is independent Dan Osborn -> stored as p_I / 'I'.
Wikipedia rating strings are kept as published (e.g. 'Lean D flip' = leans Democratic and would flip the seat). Inside Elections' own wording ('Tilt Democrat') is under rating_direct.
FiftyPlusOne numbers read from its public SvelteKit page-data endpoint (__data.json), raw extract in veri/kaynak-ham/fiftyplusone-senate-forecast.json.
